issues.legal_issue: The requirement to give public notice of the substance of a preliminary land-acquisition notification at convenient places in the locality is mandatory, and its breach invalidates the acquisition proceedings.
material_facts: The acquisition authority did not give the required public notice of the substance of the preliminary notification at convenient places in the locality.
The later notification giving particulars of the land was issued after the stage at which the authority could enter and survey the land.
The landowners challenged the acquisition proceedings on the ground that the required public notice had not been given.
issues.conclusion: The public-notice requirement was mandatory, and non-compliance made the acquisition proceedings void; the awards could not be given effect.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953, requires the Collector to give public notice of the substance of the preliminary notification at convenient places in the locality. Under section 4(2), that notice is a condition precedent to an authorised officer’s entry onto the land. The later notice under section 5(2), which provides particulars of the land, serves a different purpose and does not replace the earlier notice. The Court distinguished Babu Barkya Thakur v. State of Bombay, which concerned a formal defect in a notification rather than failure to give the required public notice, and said that Somavanti v. State of Punjab did not bear on this issue. The Court applied the principle that compulsory-acquisition powers must be strictly construed and that ‘shall’ is ordinarily mandatory where that construction accords with the statutory purpose and consequences of breach.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government pursued a proceeding to acquire land compulsorily.
predicates.collector_did_not_give_locality_notice: The Collector did not give public notice of the substance of the preliminary acquisition notification at convenient places in the locality.
predicates.later_particulars_notice_served_a_differ: A later notice provided particulars of the land after the earlier stage at which notice was intended to inform the owner before entry onto the land.

issues.definition: When a compulsory land-acquisition proceeding lacks the required locality notice, a later notice serving a different purpose does not prevent the proceeding from being void.

issues.legal_issue: A constitutional writ challenge to acquisition proceedings is not barred as belated when the challengers objected to the authority’s jurisdiction from the outset and applied soon after learning that awards had been made.
material_facts: The landowners objected to the officer’s jurisdiction and then stopped participating in the acquisition proceedings.
They learned of the awards only shortly before filing their writ petition.
They filed the petition promptly after learning that the awards had been made.
issues.conclusion: The challenge was not brought after such inordinate delay as to preclude the High Court from exercising its jurisdiction under Article 226.
issues.legal_principle: In considering whether to refuse relief under Article 226 for delay, the Court distinguished a party who submits to a tribunal’s jurisdiction and raises an objection only after an adverse decision from challengers who questioned jurisdiction from the outset and applied soon after learning of the awards. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: The challengers sought relief from a court through a constitutional writ petition.
predicates.jurisdiction_objected_to_from_outset: The challengers questioned the authority’s jurisdiction from the beginning of the proceedings.
predicates.challengers_did_not_participate_after_ob: The challengers stopped taking part in the proceedings after objecting to jurisdiction.
predicates.petition_filed_soon_after_learning_of_aw: The challengers filed their petition shortly after learning that the award had been made.

issues.definition: A constitutional writ challenge is not barred by inordinate delay when the challengers objected to jurisdiction from the outset, ceased participating after objecting, and petitioned soon after learning of the award.
